title: How different is an "engineered" genome? A diff against the zebrafish reference, set beside natural divergence
what_an_engineered_genome_is_here: Not a full genome. It is a short list of edits to the zebrafish reference (GRCz11). The winged zebrafish is a real animal (genotype/compare-2x2.json panel B); the truly flying fish is hypothetical (genotype/flier-genome.json), whose own verdict is that no route reaches the requirement.

kinds.nucleotides_changed: not given in the fetched sources; a T->K codon change needs at least 1 nucleotide

kinds.kind: structural, cis-regulatory inversion placing prrx1a regulatory sequence upstream of kcnh2a; coding sequence unchanged, heterozygous
kinds.nucleotides_changed: inversion size not given in the fetched sources; 0 amino acids changed
kinds.protein_identity_change: none (0 amino acids changed); the effect is ectopic expression

hypothetical_flier.source: genotype/flier-genome.json item 1 candidate_routes (coding routes with a named protein change and direction "increase"), plus the untested lat4a F326L import (compare-2x2 panel D logic)
not_modelled_here: kcnk5b exon-5 truncations (no single site given)
item 2 muscle: mstn knockout reported in red sea bream, not a zebrafish edit with a site
item 3 oxygen delivery: no genetic route exists
item 4 air breathing: routes are anatomical and correlative, no site-level edit
kcnh2a regulatory inversion (as above: no amino-acid change)

protein_effects.edit: hhip uki hu418B Y295* nonsense (loss of function; largest measured pectoral fin area increase, +65%)
Cx43 T154A dominant negative (delivered as a transgene in the source, not as an edit of the locus)
lat4a F326L, the flying-fish/gliding-halfbeak residue placed into zebrafish (HYPOTHETICAL: never engineered or tested in any species)

hypothetical_flier.verdict_carried_from_flier_genome: No requirement has a route that reaches it; this list is the edits one could name, not a design that would fly.

context_natural_divergence.label: median orthologue protein identity of zebrafish to each species ACROSS THE PROJECT CAUSAL-CHAIN GENES with Ensembl orthologues (not a genome-wide measurement)
context_natural_divergence.method: Biopython PairwiseAligner global, BLOSUM62, gap open -10, extend -0.5; identity = identical / aligned residue pairs; differences = mismatches + positions in indels

headline: The winged zebrafish differs from its reference by 2 edited loci and 1 amino acid. In just the 37 causal-chain proteins with medaka orthologues, zebrafish and medaka (same class, different orders) differ by 7300 amino-acid substitutions (16054 positions counting indels) (median identity 79.2%); zebrafish and a bat (Myotis) by 10205 substitutions in 33 proteins (median 74.0%); zebrafish and human by 10765 substitutions in 37 proteins. A handful of edits against thousands of differences in a few dozen proteins, and these are only the coding differences in a tiny gene sample: the genome-wide difference, coding and non-coding, was not measured here and is necessarily larger.
